name: stroke overview
title: A sudden focal deficit runs the stroke protocol: glucose, NIH Stroke Scale and localization, then a non-contrast CT; no blood means an ischemic stroke (CT angiogram and perfusion, tPA within 4.5 hours, thrombectomy for a proximal large-vessel occlusion with a mismatch) or a TIA (CT, ASA, TIA clinic), both followed by secondary prevention chosen by cause; blood means an intracerebral hemorrhage (cause by site, BP under 160/110, hold antithrombotics) or a subarachnoid hemorrhage (vessel imaging, neurosurgery)

root.title: Sudden focal neurological deficit: STROKE PROTOCOL · TIME IS BRAIN
lines: point-of-care glucose (low sugar mimics a stroke) · 2 IV lines, labs (INR, creatinine, CBC) · NIH Stroke Scale
LOCALIZE before you look at the scan: where to look for early change, which vessel (posterior → ALWAYS CTA: missed basilar thrombosis → locked-in), what is incidental
door to imaging under 25 min · door to needle under 60 min · history + meds decide cause and tPA risk
NON-CONTRAST CT first: any hemorrhage is an ABSOLUTE contraindication to tPA

groups.title: BLOOD: HEMORRHAGIC
lines: may not follow a territory · more often with a headache

head: h
Ischemic stroke
large vessel occlusion, or small vessel (lacunar)
clue: • LEFT MCA: aphasia + right face, arm > leg
• RIGHT MCA: left neglect, anosognosia + left face, arm > leg
• ACA: opposite leg · PCA: opposite hemianopsia
• BASILAR: eye movement palsy, crossed sensory, vertigo
• LACUNAR: clumsy hand-dysarthria · pure motor (face = arm = leg) · pure sensory · ataxic hemiparesis · sensorimotor
case: 57 y slumps at breakfast · eyes forced RIGHT · left hemianopsia, left face (forehead spared) + arm + leg plegic · ignores own left arm · dysarthria, no aphasia → RIGHT MCA
inv: dead brain · over 1/3 of MCA → no tPA · more change, more tPA bleeding
case: CT normal except right MCA DOT sign
• perfusion mismatch = salvageable PENUMBRA (stunned, still viable, around the dead core)
tx: bad
First check: NO tPA if ANY
• hemorrhage now or ever · SAH symptoms, seizure at onset
• BP over 185/110 despite treatment
• INR over 1.4 · PTT over 40 s · platelets under 100,000
• factor Xa inhibitor in 24-48 h · glucose under 3 or over 22
• stroke or serious head trauma under 3 months · major surgery under 14 days · GI or GU bleed under 21 days
• arterial puncture (non-compressible) or LP under 7 days
~ caution: pregnancy, pericarditis, endocarditis
ok
tPA up to 4.5 h, the EARLIER the better
• 0.9 mg/kg: 10% bolus over 1 min, rest over 1 h
• bleed risk 6%: reperfused, ischemic vessels leak
• +13% minimal or no disability (NNT 7.7)
• only 10-20% are candidates (time, unwitnessed onset, anticoagulated, too mild, hemorrhage)
ok
Thrombectomy
• proximal occlusion + mismatch, even WITHOUT tPA (anticoagulated, over 4.5 h)
• under 5% are candidates · stent retriever, sedation or anesthesia

head: h
Transient ischemic attack (TIA)
usually under 1 hour · NO infarct
clue: • case: 65 y smoker, 10 min right face droop + hand weakness · BP 138/88, exam normal, no murmur, no bruit
• listen for a murmur (cardioembolic) and carotid bruit
inv: echo · Holter · CTA or carotid Dopplers · lipids, glucose, BP · then manage as secondary prevention
tx: ok
Start ASA
already on ASA → add clopidogrel for 21 days

head: h
Intracerebral hemorrhage
bleeding into the brain
clue: in order: hypertension · amyloid · tumour · AVM, cavernoma, aneurysm · coagulopathy
case: 57 y, sudden right-sided tingling, can't walk · BP 185/90 · right face, arm, leg weak, dense right sensory loss → LEFT basal ganglia bleed
white matter just under frontal, parietal, occipital cortex
inv: also tumour (metastasis) · AVM, cavernoma, aneurysm · coagulopathy
tx: bad
NO tPA
• BP under 160/110 (some say under 140/90)
• HOLD all antiplatelets and anticoagulants
• MECHANICAL DVT prophylaxis
• surgery very rarely: only raised pressure + accessible clot
• good prognosis if no shift or herniation
after: repeat CT · no clot extension → heparin prophylaxis · rehabilitation

head: h
Subarachnoid hemorrhage
ruptured aneurysm, in most (or trauma)
clue: • 41 y: sudden, explosive, worst headache of her life
inv: CTA or MRA to find the aneurysm
tx: ok
Admit to NEUROSURGERY
coil or clip, by the aneurysm's shape and site

rows: SECONDARY PREVENTION, chosen by the CAUSE
admit to the stroke unit: BP watch, telemetry, echo, imaging at 24 h, bed rest 24 h, nothing by mouth until a swallowing assessment · PT, OT, social work
no bleed at 24 h → ASA, DVT prophylaxis, statin · rehabilitation beats even tPA · most recovery in 3 months, some up to a year
• CARDIOEMBOLIC (atrial fibrillation, valve) → ANTICOAGULATE, ~2 weeks after
• all other causes → ASA 81 mg · clopidogrel if ASA fails
• symptomatic carotid stenosis over 70% → endarterectomy or stent · under 70% or asymptomatic → medical
• BP under 140/90 · high-dose statin · glucose · smoking · activity, diet, weight
• ASA + clopidogrel for some high-risk patients

panels.title: Ischemic causes → directed workup
items: artery to artery: carotid, intracranial, aorta → carotid imaging (anterior) or vertebrobasilar (posterior): MRA, CTA, Doppler
CARDIOEMBOLIC → echo (TTE, TEE, bubble study for PFO/ASD) · telemetry, Holter for atrial fibrillation
hypoperfusion → WATERSHED infarcts · laminar necrosis of the cortical ribbon

panels.title: Acute weakness: stroke or mimic?
items: ischemic stroke: FOLLOWS a vascular territory
hemorrhage: may not follow one · more often headache
migraine: weakness MARCHES, slow on and off, minutes · young women
Todd's paresis: unwitnessed seizure · improves over hours
hypoglycemia (esp. old strokes) · psychogenic: inconsistent, better distracted

panels.title: Risk factors + primary prevention
items: modifiable: hypertension, diabetes, cholesterol, smoking, atrial fibrillation, heart disease
sedentary, obesity, cocaine or amphetamines, postpartum, bleeding disorders, anticoagulants
fixed: age, sex, ethnicity, family history
primary: treat risk factors · low-dose ASA if several · atrial fibrillation + high CHADS2 → anticoagulate
